reason: From n ≡ 1 mod 2d we get n = 1 + 2dt, so n is odd, and any common divisor of n and 2d divides 1; hence gcd(n,2d)=1. Then no factor 1+ζ^{dj} can vanish for an nth root ζ, because that would force (-1)^n=1. Finally, any nonconstant common divisor of U_{d,n} and M_n would have a complex root α; since M_n(α)=0, α is a nontrivial nth root of unity, but U_{d,n} does not vanish at such points, contradiction.
